description: The hand-verified expected result for the positive Opengrep SARIF fixture. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.

fixture.excerpt_note: The eight results are byte-identical members of the raw artifact's 1322 results: the fixture is unmodified captured output. It is never edited to suit these rows; these rows are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256 above makes visible.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Every uri in this fixture is already root-relative, and the recorded path base for opengrep is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the uri unchanged. These rows therefore hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the opengrep entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.uri_base_id_walk_consequence: With no run.originalUriBaseIds the SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.4.4 procedure cannot complete -- the documented producer gap -- and that outcome is eligible for the metadata-backed fallback, so each path resolves against the runner-recorded base rather than being rejected.
resolution_context.severity_source: No result in this fixture states a level, and no rule carries properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so every severity_native is the level its own rule states under defaultConfiguration.level and every severity_norm comes from the SARIF level table: error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per path kind and one severity_basis_* per severity basis.
counters_note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool -- multi_location_records, multi_valued_cwe_records, multi_valued_cve_records and non_filesystem_paths -- are all 0 for this fixture: every result carries exactly one location, no rule carries more than one CWE identifier, no rule string carries a CVE identifier, and every path names a file inside the scanned tree.

corroboration.note: The eight records this fixture excerpts also appear in the committed dataset, and every one of the twelve fields agrees with the rows below. That is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values: each value here was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply.
